conversations.say: Arden, before we toast fifteen years of R on a printing floor that smells more like PR than press grease, let's look at the archive. I want the intake report and your expense records side-by-side with my letter packet.
conversations.offer: Early newsroom history and access to inspect the First R Letter packet.
conversations.request: The full, qualified intake and expense record without ceremonial spin.

conversations.say: Tessa, you've always argued that celebrated bylines bury the collaborative machinery beneath them. Tell me plainly: which parts of my old newsroom stories erased actual collective labor?
conversations.offer: My perspective on early newsroom workflow and editorial protection.
conversations.request: Your honest critique of how individual authorship myths function.

public_statement: Fifteen years ago, a stranger brought a letter to my desk that started something real. If people want to turn history into a committee meeting today, they'll have to answer to the voice on the page.
goal_progress: Initiated contact with Arden regarding archive and expense records.
Engaged Tessa on the collective labor critique.
reasoning_summary: Opened Section 1 by confronting Arden for archive records and engaging Tessa on collective labor vs individual authorship, establishing Frankie's defensive yet transactional stance on the origin story.
